summary: Fenticonazole nitrate is a broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal used topically and intravaginally to treat vulvovaginal candidiasis and superficial dermatomycoses. It is fungicidal against Candida and dermatophytes with additional activity against some gram-positive bacteria. Systemic absorption from skin and vaginal mucosa is minimal. It is not approved by the US FDA but is marketed in Europe, India and other markets under SmPC/BNF guidance.
indications: Dermatophytoses (tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea pedis)
Superficial fungal skin infections with secondary gram-positive bacterial involvement

dosage.d: 600 mg pessary as a single dose
dosage.n: May repeat after 3 days if needed

dosage.t: Once daily at night for 3 nights
Once daily at night for 3 nights

admin: Insert vaginal pessary high into the vagina at bedtime, lying down
Wash and dry skin before applying cream; rub in gently
Wash hands before and after application
Complete the full course even if symptoms resolve early
Avoid contact with the eyes; for external/intravaginal use only
moa: Fenticonazole is an imidazole that inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. The resulting ergosterol depletion and accumulation of toxic sterol precursors disrupt the fungal cell membrane. It additionally impairs cytochrome oxidase and peroxidase activity and secretion of proteases, giving fungicidal activity against Candida and dermatophytes.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to fenticonazole or other imidazole antifungals
Hypersensitivity to any excipient of the preparation
relative: First trimester of pregnancy unless clearly necessary
Use during menstruation (vaginal preparations may be less effective)

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not established. Avoid in the first trimester and use only if the expected benefit outweighs risk; if used in later pregnancy, insert pessaries by hand rather than with an applicator. Follow specialist/SmPC advice.
lact: Systemic absorption after topical or vaginal use is minimal, so significant excretion into breast milk is unlikely. Data are limited; use with caution and only when clearly needed.
renal: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption after topical/intravaginal application is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption after topical/intravaginal application is negligible.

major: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions expected with topical/vaginal use
moderate: Latex condoms and diaphragms - vaginal preparations may damage latex and reduce contraceptive reliability
minor: Other intravaginal products used concurrently - may interfere with local efficacy
interactions.food: Not applicable for topical or intravaginal use.
interactions.diagnostics: No known interference with laboratory tests.

common: Local burning or stinging at application site
Erythema or itching of treated skin/mucosa
emergency: Signs of severe allergic reaction (widespread rash, facial/throat swelling, breathing difficulty)

monitoring: Clinical response over the treatment course
Reassess diagnosis if no improvement or recurrence after a full course
Consider partner treatment in recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis
counsel: Use exactly as directed; complete the full course even if better
For vaginal use, insert at bedtime and remain lying down
Avoid intercourse, tampons and douching during treatment if advised
Latex condoms/diaphragms may be weakened - use alternative contraception during and for several days after
Stop and seek advice if severe irritation or allergic reaction occurs
pk: Local antifungal action begins shortly after application
Acts locally; negligible systemic plasma concentrations
Not clinically relevant - minimal systemic absorption
Single 600 mg pessary maintains local effect; dose 1-2 times daily for cream
Store below 25-30 C, protected from heat; keep out of reach of children
pearls: Not FDA-approved; pending clinical review. Marketed in Europe/India per EMA/SmPC and BNF guidance.
Broad-spectrum imidazole with fungicidal activity against Candida, dermatophytes and some gram-positive bacteria
Single-dose 600 mg pessary offers a convenient regimen for uncomplicated vaginal thrush
Damages latex - advise alternative contraception during and after vaginal use
Recurrent or refractory candidiasis warrants reassessment and consideration of partner/oral therapy
missed: For the skin cream, apply the missed dose as soon as remembered and continue the usual schedule; do not double up. For an intravaginal course, insert the missed dose as soon as remembered and complete the remaining nights as directed.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical or intravaginal use given negligible systemic absorption. Accidental ingestion may cause gastrointestinal upset; manage supportively and contact a poison control center. Remove excess applied product by washing.
